comment:
Read at commit 8a38d02 (HEAD). Two commits carry 2.0.1 — eee00ef and 8a38d02 — and the only difference between them is README.md, so src/ and res/ are identical and nothing needed settling against the installed build.

The CV inputs do not add to the knobs, they write to them: src/IPQ.cpp:74 and :77 call setValue on the ParamQuantity every sample, so the knob turns under the cable and its own setting is lost. The README's 'Each interval can be changed via CV IN' does not say this.

The whole quantizer sits inside a test for both IN and OUT being connected (src/IPQ.cpp:84). The TRIGGER output is written inside that same test, so with OUT unpatched TRIGGER is never updated. The README describes TRIGGER without mentioning the dependency.

The interval test at src/IPQ.cpp:88 compares the raw input against the last quantized output, not against the last input, so the distance is measured from the note being sent.

The search loop at src/IPQ.cpp:89-98 runs i from 0 to 12 inclusive against a fractional pitch, so the octave above is a candidate as well as the twelve semitones; the result is ordinary chromatic quantization.

The README says +/-0V is unison and +/-10V is a Major 7th. Negative voltages are not symmetrical: setValue clamps at the bottom of the 0 to 11 range, so every negative voltage gives unison.

The two interval displays are LedDisplay widgets with no ParamWidget behind them, so they have no census position and no click can reach them.

The module adds nothing to its right-click menu.
